description:
The frequent list (fuel.ts:44-64) groups on lower(trim(label)) and takes the newest entry's macros. It is good, and it is fragile in one way: "chicken breast" and "Chicken Breast 200g" are two different foods to it, and the macros drift with whatever was last typed.

The user's stated requirement is explicitly NOT exact meal logging — no food database, no barcodes, no 12-million-row catalog. So the right shape is a small personal food memory, not an integration: a saved item is a label plus macros per unit, where the unit is the user's own ("1 scoop", "100 g", "1 breast"). Logging it = pick item, pick quantity, done; the entry still writes absolute grams and kcal so history and targets are untouched.

Scope: a fuel_item table (userId, label, unit, proteinGPerUnit, caloriesPerUnit, archivedAt), CRUD under /api/fuel/items, "save this as an item" on any logged entry, and the quick-add row reading from items first and falling back to today's frequent-label derivation for anything not saved.

Do this AFTER T-045 through T-047 (quantity, edit, back-date). Those fix logging that is currently impossible; this one makes logging that already works faster.

FUEL PAGE (2026-09-26): a fuel_item also carries carbsGPerUnit and fatGPerUnit, nullable exactly as T-052 makes them on entries, so do T-052 first. The My foods screen lists items by how often they were logged and edits one in place. It shows "macros add up to N kcal · you entered M" as a hint, never a correction. It also has a "Logged often, not saved" section that offers to save a frequent label. Editing an item never rewrites entries already logged. Mockup: https://claude.ai/artifact/CD3dbZS6upyEbpCcv25c2g (Foods).
title: Personal food memory: saved items with a unit and per-unit macros
